title: ChatGPT vs Claude vs Copilot: which should your team roll out?
description: ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot for a 40-500 person firm: prices read 26 Nov 2026, seat caps, data and admin controls, and who each fits.
topic: ChatGPT vs Claude vs Microsoft Copilot for your team
job: pick which AI assistant to roll out to staff
verdict: Pick Copilot if your mail, files and meetings live in Microsoft 365 and you want audit logs there[^29][^34].
Pick ChatGPT if you run Google Workspace or a mixed stack and may grow past 150 seats[^17][^18].
Pick Claude if your team works in long documents and spreadsheets and has 150 people or fewer[^3][^16].
Run two if you're on Microsoft 365: Copilot Chat costs nothing extra; buy ChatGPT or Claude for heavy users[^31][^17].

summary: All three keep business chats out of model training by default[^7][^20][^32]. Copilot works inside Microsoft 365 and sees what each person can already open; ChatGPT and Claude reach your files through admin-approved connectors[^31][^12][^26]. What makes or breaks it: who controls access and who checks output[^51][^33].

cells: Sidebar in Excel and Google Sheets. OpenAI says to review changed cells before sharing[^24].

recipes.name: 1. Microsoft 365 firm, 40-150 staff
recipes.when: Your mail, files and Teams meetings already live in Microsoft 365[^29]. Start with Copilot Chat for everyone, then buy paid seats for proven heavy users[^31][^29].
flow: IT admin: turn on Copilot Chat for all staff at no extra cost
IT admin: run Microsoft's readiness check and fix overshared SharePoint sites
COO: write a one-page use policy: what data goes in, who reviews what
Ops lead: pick 10-30 heavy email and meeting users in one unit or site for paid Copilot Business
IT admin: set a spending limit for per-use agents such as Cowork
Department heads: name a reviewer for anything that leaves the firm
Ops lead: at day 60-90, add seats or reassign idle ones
recipes.cost: 25 paid seats × $21 × 12 = $6,300 a year at list, read 26 Nov 2026[^29]. Bought by 31 Dec 2026, the $18 promo makes year one $5,400[^29].

recipes.name: 2. Google Workspace or mixed-stack firm, 40-150 staff
recipes.when: Your mail and files sit in Gmail and Drive, or across several tools[^14][^59]. ChatGPT Business and Claude Team cost the same $20 a seat billed yearly, so pilot one against the other[^17][^3].
flow: IT or owner: create the workspace, verify the domain, turn on company sign-in (SSO)
IT: switch on only Drive, Gmail and Calendar, and keep approval before send
Ops lead: time three repeat tasks first, so there is a before-and-after number
Ops lead: run a 60-90 day pilot with 10-20 people in one unit or site, on monthly billing
Department heads: name who checks output before it leaves the team
COO and finance: at day 60-90, move to yearly billing; buy Premium only for heavy agent users
recipes.cost: Pilot: 15 seats × $25 × 3 months = $1,125 on either plan[^17][^3]. Rollout: 100 Standard seats billed yearly cost $24,000 on either, read 26 Nov 2026[^17][^3].

recipes.name: 3. Regulated firm, or 150-500 staff
recipes.when: Claude Team stops at 150 seats, new ChatGPT Business workspaces at 200 and Copilot Business at 300[^3][^18][^29]. Go to an enterprise tier if you need audit logs, automatic offboarding (SCIM) or retention control[^5][^17].
flow: Compliance lead: list hard needs: health-data contract (BAA), retention period, legal hold
COO: get written quotes with seat minimums and usage terms
Finance: model Claude Enterprise usage and set firm and per-user spend limits
IT: connect automatic add and remove (SCIM) to your identity system
Compliance lead: confirm where chat logs land: Purview for Copilot, audit logs or the Compliance API for the others
Department heads: keep sign-off rules for each role
recipes.cost: 300 seats: Claude Enterprise seat fees are $72,000 a year plus usage; Microsoft 365 Copilot is $108,000[^2][^30]. ChatGPT Enterprise is quote-only; third parties report about $60 a seat a month[^17][^28].

humanRole: The COO sets the usage policy and owns the rollout; IT decides what the assistant can read. Claude and ChatGPT admins switch on each connector, and Copilot sees only what each person can already open[^12][^22][^31].
A person presses send: Claude blocks Team users from auto-approving send tools, and ChatGPT may ask before posting to Teams[^13][^25]. OWASP advises human confirmation for high-stakes actions[^50].
The owner of each number checks it, such as the controller for finance work. Both spreadsheet add-ins tell users to review changed cells, and NIST advises checking output[^24][^16][^51].
Compliance owns the record. Copilot logs each interaction to Purview Audit, Microsoft's compliance log, while Claude and ChatGPT audit logs need their enterprise tiers[^34][^5][^23].

example.input: Illustrative: a 120-person distributor on Microsoft 365. Ops coordinators paste supplier price lists into personal ChatGPT or Claude accounts, which may train on chats depending on a user setting[^20][^8]. In one survey, 68% of enterprise workers used personal AI accounts and 57% entered sensitive data[^52].
example.output: After: all 120 get Copilot Chat at no extra cost, and 15 ops and finance leads get Copilot Business for $3,780 a year[^31][^29]. IT fixes overshared SharePoint sites first[^33]. Two pricing analysts get Claude Team or ChatGPT Business seats, and the buyer checks every price change before it reaches a supplier[^16][^24].

watchOuts: Leaving staff on personal accounts: 68% of surveyed workers use them, and personal ChatGPT and Claude plans may train on chats[^52][^20][^8]. Fix: buy a business plan and move people over.
Switching on Copilot before fixing file permissions: it sees whatever each person can open[^31][^33]. Fix: run Microsoft's readiness check and clean up overshared sites first[^38][^39].

Buying seats nobody uses: firms leave 36% of software licences unused, and AI use is 'widespread but shallow'[^53][^47]. Fix: pilot first; Claude Team seats can be reassigned but removals aren't refunded[^4].
Budgeting seats, not usage: Copilot Cowork bills per use, and Claude Enterprise bills all usage at API rates[^29][^5]. Fix: set firm and per-user spend limits before launch[^5].
Trusting it on analysis it's weak at: a UK government test found Copilot's Excel analysis slower and lower quality[^54]. Fix: name which tasks always get a human check[^51].

Letting agents act on email and files unchecked: hidden instructions in a document or email can hijack an assistant, OWASP's top AI risk[^49]. Fix: keep approval on for send and write actions[^10][^50].

faq.q: Is ChatGPT Business or Claude Team better for a small team?
faq.a: On price they tie: $20 a seat billed yearly and $25 monthly on both, read 26 Nov 2026[^17][^3]. Claude Team caps at 150 seats and ChatGPT Business at 200[^3][^18]. Pick on where your files live and which one your pilot group prefers.

faq.q: Claude or Copilot for a 40-person company on Microsoft 365?
faq.a: Copilot, if most work is email, meetings and SharePoint: it searches them directly and logs to Purview[^31][^34]. Claude reaches the same data through a connector a Microsoft admin approves, and suits heavy document and Excel work[^12][^16].
Yes, in most US business accounts: Claude models are on by default in Copilot, Researcher and Cowork[^36][^37]. Admins can turn them off, and they sit outside Microsoft's EU Data Boundary[^36].

faq.q: What is the difference between ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork?
faq.a: Little in kind: both are agent modes that run multi-step tasks and hand back files[^21][^11]. Both draw on the business seat's usage; Copilot's Cowork bills per use on top[^60][^3][^29].

faq.q: Will ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot train on our company data?
faq.a: Not by default on business plans, per all three vendors[^20][^7][^32]. Personal plans differ: ChatGPT and Claude may train on those chats unless the user opts out[^20][^8].

faq.q: Is Copilot safer than Claude for a company rollout?
faq.a: Neither trains on business data by default, so the gap is records[^7][^32]. Copilot logs every interaction to Purview Audit; Claude and ChatGPT audit logs need their enterprise tiers[^34][^5][^23].

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy one of these when the job is everyday drafting, summarizing and spreadsheet work for many staff[^55]. MIT found bought tools reached deployment about twice as often as internal builds[^55]. Over half of US businesses on Ramp already pay for AI this way[^48].
buyVsBuild.build: Build on a vendor's API when your own data or a fixed process is the edge, such as document intake tied to your systems[^55]. Claude Enterprise already bills usage at API rates, which blurs the line[^5].

pickElse: You run Google Workspace and needs are light: Business Standard, at $14 a user a month billed yearly, includes Gemini in Gmail, Docs and Meet[^40]. Google says it doesn't train on your data without permission[^41].
You're on Microsoft 365 and testing the water: start with Copilot Chat at no extra cost[^31]. Buy paid seats once usage shows who needs them[^53].
You need one repeat process fixed, such as invoice intake: a purpose-built tool beats a general assistant[^55].
Staff won't use it yet: fix the task list and training first[^47]. In one large field study, a three-hour onboarding came first, and newer staff gained most[^42].

offer.heading: Not sure which assistant to roll out to your team?
offer.body: In 30 minutes we look at where your files live, your seat count and your data rules. You leave with a pick, a year-one cost and a pilot plan.

reviews.notes: Wants one pick to forward, a cost and a first step. Bottom line gives a pick per stack and size; recipes give costs and first steps; the COO now owns policy and rollout in the human-role block.
